title: Search the product catalogue
ticket: Search works for simple words like 'mouse', but searching for 'usb c & hdmi' shows an error, even though we sell that adapter.
hints: Compare the request the code sends for 'mouse' with the one it sends for 'usb c & hdmi'. Look at how the URL is built.
The search term goes into the URL exactly as typed. In a URL, `&` starts a new query parameter and spaces are not allowed, so the server never receives the full term.
Encode the term before putting it in the URL: `'/api/search?q=' + encodeURIComponent(term)`, or build the query with `URLSearchParams`.
theory: Some characters have special meaning in a URL: `&` separates query parameters, `#` starts the fragment, `?` starts the query and `+` can mean a space. Any value you put into a URL, especially user input, must be percent-encoded with `encodeURIComponent()`, or built with `URLSearchParams`, which encodes for you. This bug is a classic in support tickets because it only appears for some inputs: everything works until a customer types an ampersand, an accent or a slash.
